title: privacy-erase
description: The erasure contract. A DSAR (GDPR art.17 / PDPL) is only complete when EVERY system holding the person's data has answered — so completion is DERIVED from acknowledgements, never declared. Any service, in any language, on any platform participates by implementing ONE endpoint that accepts this request and returns this ack, and by being registered as a target (a name=base_url config entry + a data-map row). The compliance dispatcher then drives it. There is no registry of 'our' services in code: base-services' own ten implement exactly this contract and are registered exactly this way — they are the reference implementation, not a special case.

request.title: erase request
request.description: POST {target_base_url}{PRIVACY_ERASE_PATH} — default path /internal/privacy/erase. Authenticated as a service (internal token by default; a target may require its own credentials). MUST be IDEMPOTENT: a DSAR retries, so erasing an already-erased subject is a no-op that still acks.

tenant.description: The tenant whose data is in scope. A target MUST scope its deletion to this tenant — never erase across tenants.

subject.description: The platform's subject reference for this tenant — the exact value the records key on. Passed VERBATIM and matched VERBATIM: never re-hash it (we hashed an already-hashed subject once, matched zero rows, and got a clean 'erased' over the wrong id). Pseudonymise only for your ACK's subject_ref, never to match.

subject_kind.description: OPTIONAL. The KIND of identifier `subject` is — e.g. 'pseudonym', 'phone_hash', 'internal_id'. Absent/empty means the caller did not qualify it and you match the verbatim value as usual. When present, and you index your records by a DIFFERENT kind that you cannot match this value against, you MUST refuse explicitly: return the ack with unrecognized_subject_kind=true (see the ack). Matching a kind you do not index against zero rows and acking 'erased' is a false completion — the worst lie this system can tell. This field is metadata ABOUT the subject; it is never a second value to match on.

action.description: Which right is being exercised. A target that only supports erase may refuse export explicitly (never silently).

request_id.description: The DSAR id, echoed so a target can make its own work idempotent and can push a late ack back to /internal/compliance/dsar/{request_id}/target-ack.

ack.title: erase acknowledgement
ack.description: Returned with HTTP 200 when the work is DONE (the dispatcher records the ack for you). Return HTTP 202 instead if erasure is slow/asynchronous — then POST this same body to /internal/compliance/dsar/{request_id}/target-ack when finished. Anything else is a failure and will be retried with backoff; after max attempts the target is marked FAILED and the DSAR stays INCOMPLETE and visible. NEVER return 200 for work you did not do: a false 'she was erased' is the worst lie this system can tell.

service.description: Your service's stable name — MUST match the name it is registered under, because acks are keyed by (request_id, service, category).

category.description: The data category you hold (e.g. invoices, user_files, messages). Matches your data-map row; a service holding several categories acks each.

subject_ref.description: A PSEUDONYM of the subject (salted hash), never the raw identifier — the ack itself must not become a new copy of the personal data.

erased.description: What was deleted, as counted facts (e.g. "files:12"). Empty is legitimate — say so with already_absent or retained.

retained.description: What SURVIVED, each with its legal basis. 'We kept it' is always an answer with a reason attached, never a silence — a DSAR that cannot say why data survived has not answered the person.

basis.description: The lawful basis for keeping it, e.g. legal_obligation, consent_proof.

why.description: Plain-language reason a regulator (or the person) can read.

already_absent.description: True when this service held nothing for the subject. An honest 'nothing here' — distinct from a failure, and distinct from having erased something. The dispatcher records it DISTINCTLY: a zero-row 'erasure' is never silently a clean full success (if every target says this, the subject id was probably wrong).

truncated.description: True when you erased only PART of the subject's rows this call (a bounded batch, a scan cap) and MORE REMAINS. Return HTTP 200 with this set: the dispatcher records PARTIAL — you stay UNACKED and the erase re-dispatches (idempotently) until a call returns WITHOUT truncated. NEVER omit it for work that is not finished: a target that erased 5,000 of 40,000 and did not say truncated is recorded as fully done.

unrecognized_subject_kind.description: True when the request carried a subject_kind you do NOT index by, so you could not match the value against any records. This is an explicit REFUSAL, not an erasure: the dispatcher records it FAILED (never acked), so the DSAR stays open and visible rather than closing over a subject you never found. Set this instead of returning already_absent (which asserts you looked and held nothing) — you did not look, because you could not. Any service in any language is safe by returning this flag: the DSAR-protecting classification lives in the dispatcher, not in you.
